title: Employee incentive schemes
subject: This guide sets out ASIC's guidance on when it will give relief from the disclosure, licensing, advertising, hawking, managed investment scheme, and on-sale provisions of the Corporations Act 2001 for an employee incentive scheme.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 and explains ASIC's policy for facilitating employee incentive schemes. It is intended for listed and unlisted bodies that wish to offer financial products to employees under such schemes, and outlines the conditions under which ASIC will provide class order relief.
ruling: ASIC states that it will provide class order relief for employee incentive schemes subject to specific conditions. The relief covers who can make offers (listed bodies and their associated bodies corporate), who can participate (employees and certain contractors), what financial products can be offered (e.g., shares, options), and the structures that can be used. The guide sets out general conditions for relief, including disclosure and reporting requirements, and distinguishes between listed bodies (Sections B–F) and unlisted bodies (Section G). ASIC's approach is to facilitate employee share ownership while ensuring investor protection and market integrity.
